fields.description: Enter one JSON object. Worked example: {"mode": "fixed", "fields": ["doc_id: str", "page_count: int", "note: str?"]}. Every entry in "fields" is the string "name: type", where type is one of str, int, float, bool, any, and a trailing "?" marks the field optional ("note: str?" is an optional string). Field names must be valid Python identifiers — write "doc_id", not "doc-id" or "doc.id". Modes: "fixed" accepts exactly these fields, "flexible" accepts these plus any extras the data carries, and "observed" infers every field from the data — with "observed" leave "fields" out entirely ({"mode": "observed"}).
fields.label: Schema
fields.name: schema

fields.description: Fields this transform requires in input. Used for DAG validation to catch missing field errors at config time. For templates, use elspeth.core.templates.extract_jinja2_fields() to discover fields.
fields.label: Required Input Fields
fields.name: required_input_fields

fields.description: The reference table as raw text. Written by the settings loader from 'reference_file' on the CLI, or by inline_content blob substitution on the web. Authoring it directly inline is legal but usually means a file was intended.
fields.label: Reference Content
fields.name: reference_content

fields.description: Path the reference table was loaded from. Written by the loader; used only in diagnostics.
fields.label: Reference Source
fields.name: reference_source

fields.description: How to parse reference_content. Never inferred — a blob carries no reliable type.
fields.label: Reference Format
fields.name: reference_format

fields.description: Input field whose value is matched against the reference table key.
fields.label: Key Field
fields.name: key_field

fields.description: Name of the key WITHIN each reference entry (a CSV header, or a JSON object member). Deliberately not named '*_field': it names a column of the reference table, not of the row.
fields.label: Reference Key Name
fields.name: reference_key_name

fields.description: Map of output field name to an expression over the matched entry, bound as 'ref' (for example "ref['description']" or "ref['tax']['rate']").
fields.label: Output

fields.description: What to do when the row key is absent from the table, or an output expression does not resolve against the matched entry: fail the row, write null, or write default_values.

fields.description: Per-output-field fallback values used when on_miss is 'default'.
fields.label: Default Values
